items.synopsis: IRB routed traffic is dropped when both hosts are learned on the same SP-style Layer 2 interface on EVO-PTX platforms Product- Group=evo On all Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms, IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) routed traffic is dropped when both source and destination hosts are reachable through the same Service Provider (SP)-style Layer 2 IFL (Logical Interface) and associated IRB interface.

items.category: Host path software for ACX platform
items.synopsis: The ACX-Series platforms stop sending and receiving control plane traffic. Product- Group=evo On all ACX-Series platforms running Junos Evolved Operation System (OS), the device stops sending and receiving control plane traffic and a packetio core-dump is generated while handling incorrect packets length received from ASIC.

Underlay traffic interruption due to nexthop HOLD state triggered by delayed ARP refresh Product- Group=evo On all Junos Evolved ACX platforms, underlay traffic is interrupted when ARP(Address Resolution Protocol) request packets required for refresh are dropped due to congestion or ratelimiting conditions. As a result, the nexthop entry temporarily transitions to a HOLD state in hardware even though ARP later recovers in the control plane. Traffic resumes only after the forwarding state is refreshed.

dscp-code-point under host- outbound-traffic is not enabled on PTX Product- Group=evo set class-of-service host-outbound-traffic dscp-code-point was disabled on PTX in 25.4R1. Later it was enabled in 26.2R1 and backported to 25.4R2

items.category: Junos Evolved Netstack Socket Intercept and NetIO
items.synopsis: Host-initiated dig DNS queries over UDP times out when DNS proxy is configured on Junos OS Evolved devices Product- Group=evo On all Junos OS Evolved devices, host-initiated Domain Name System (DNS) queries using User Datagram Protocol (UDP), such as queries initiated with the dig utility, will time out when DNS proxy is configured on revenue ports. DNS queries using Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) continue to succeed. Forwarding/data-plane traffic is not affected.

Incorrect MAC Reported by SNMP OID ifPhysAddress for Aggregated Ethernet Product- Group=evo On all Junos Evo platforms, For AE interfaces, the SNMP OID ifPhysAddress (iso.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.6) returns the MAC address of a bundled physical member interface instead of the manually configured logical MAC address on the AE interface, resulting in incorrect output.

The other port in a port group goes down after an RE switchover if one of the port in the port group is already down on an On Junos OS Evolved ACX7509 platforms, when one port in a channelized group (like ports 0 in a port group consisting of port 0 and port 1) is already in 'down' state in a ACX7509-FPC-16C with 16x100G-QSFP, performing a Routing Engine (RE) switchover or restarting the picd process can cause the other port in the port group to go down. This will lead to disruption of services running on the port. ACX7509 Product- Group=evo
